texts.facts: The petitioner before this Court who is one of the Directors being aggrieved by the complaint filed by State of Madhya Pradesh through Food Inspector under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 bearing Complaint Case No.2467/2011 has preferred the present petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 2. Facts of the case reveal that the company in question Dharampal Satyapal Limited is a company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 having its registered office at Delhi. The company is engaged in manufacture of masala, cold drinks, water and food masala etc. It is having consignee sale agents all over the country and one of such agent is appointed in the State of Madhya Pradesh. On 30.04.2011 an inspection was conducted at the firm working in the name of Textile of Harkawat and Company where the owner of the firm Shri Amit Harkawat was present and after giving him necessary notice for taking the sample of Rajnigandha Pan Masala after paying the requisite price for three pouches of 210 grams pack collected as sample and after completing the formalities sample was sent to the laboratory for its analysis. By letter dated 16.06.2011 the Food Inspector received the report from the food analyst whereby the sample was declared to be adulterated. The Food Inspector on 25.06.2011 sent a letter to the nominee of the company Mr. Pradeep Bobde, Godown In-charge, Indore seeking details of the licenced nominee of the company and the bills. On 11.07.2011 the General Manager of the company informed respondent No.1 that Shri Pradeep Bobde has been appointed as nominee of the company as the Officer In- charge under Section 17 read with Rule -12 (B) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules 1955. The Food Inspector also sought details from Guwahati Unit and by letter dated 29.08.2011 got to know that the nominee of the company is one Shashikant Mani Tripathi appointed as aforesaid. Thereafter the compliant has been lodged against the petitioner under Section 7/16 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954. Respondent No.1 can proceed with the concerning case only against the respondents No.2.3 and 4. 4.
